title: Assemblies, metadata, and InternalsVisibleTo
hook: A .NET assembly is a versioned unit packaging Intermediate Language (IL), metadata, and resources — not just a single class file. Metadata describes every type and member so the Common Language Runtime (CLR) can load, verify, and link code at run time.

blocks.text: An assembly (.dll or .exe) contains IL instructions, a manifest (name, version, culture), and rich metadata tables describing types, methods, fields, and attributes. Project references and NuGet packages resolve to assemblies. InternalsVisibleTo lets a friend test assembly access internal members without making them public.

entries.plainDefinition: A deployment unit of IL plus metadata, usually a .dll or .exe file.
entries.example: MyApp.Domain.dll holds domain types and their metadata.

entries.plainDefinition: Structured description of types and members stored inside the assembly.
entries.example: Reflection reads metadata to list public methods on a type.

entries.plainDefinition: Assembly-level attribute granting another assembly access to internal types.

blocks.text: Microservices share contracts via assembly references or NuGet packages — versioning and breaking changes are assembly-level concerns. Strong naming and binding redirects solve version mismatches at load time. Test projects use InternalsVisibleTo to test internal helpers without polluting public API surface.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: InternalsVisibleTo with wrong assembly name — tests fail to access internals. Mixing copy-local DLLs with mismatched versions. Assuming one .cs file equals one assembly.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: assembly load failures show as FileNotFoundException or LoaderExceptions in inner exceptions — log AssemblyLoadContext.Default.Assemblies or use Fusion Log Viewer on Windows for binding redirects. AssemblyLoadContext (ALC) separates default shared runtime assemblies from collectible plugin contexts — unload collectible ALCs after plugin hot-swap to reclaim metadata. InternalsVisibleTo requires strong-name public key token when the friend is signed. dotnet-dump !dumpassembly -all lists loaded assemblies during a memory investigation.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Test friends without public API pollution

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Equating one .cs file to one assembly — a project emits one assembly with many types. Saying AppDomain is the modern plugin story without mentioning AssemblyLoadContext. InternalsVisibleTo without PublicKey on signed friends. Loading plugins into Default ALC and expecting to unload DLLs — Default is not collectible.

interviewTakeaways: An assembly packages IL, metadata, and manifest — versioning and loading are assembly-level, not file-level.
AssemblyLoadContext isolates plugin loads; collectible ALCs enable unload without process restart.
In production, log binding failures and use deps.json alignment — version mismatches surface as FileNotFoundException at startup.
60s: Assembly is IL plus metadata plus version. Default ALC for app. Collectible ALC for plugins. InternalsVisibleTo for test friends. NuGet ships assemblies, not source.
Follow-up: when can you not unload a collectible AssemblyLoadContext?
commonPitfalls: Saying one class file equals one assembly gets you rejected — projects compile many types into one DLL.
Wrong friend assembly name in InternalsVisibleTo — tests compile but cannot access internals.
Strong answer: 'ALC for plugin isolation. Collectible for hot swap. InternalsVisibleTo keeps tests off public API. Log loader exceptions on deploy.'
